artifact.canonical_name: Computation-Accuracy Trade-Off in Service-Oriented Model-Based Control

sources.title: Computation-Accuracy Trade-Off in Service-Oriented Model-Based Control
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The paper represents control-loop elements as services so that model-based control structure can be recomposed at runtime.
Service orchestration is formulated as an A* search problem and Contextual Bayesian Optimization tunes multi-objective weights for computation-versus-control-accuracy trade-offs.
A vehicle longitudinal-velocity control case study demonstrates online performance-driven reconfiguration while considering real-time control requirements.

limitations.text: The accessible primary abstract does not expose the control-plant model, service alternatives, hardware/runtime platform, objective values, search/runtime overhead, accuracy metrics, or real-time deadline results.
The demonstrated application is a longitudinal-velocity control case and should not be generalized to all mixed-criticality vehicle functions.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Computation-Accuracy Trade-Off in Service-Oriented Model-Based Control; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The primary abstract verifies SOMC, A* orchestration, Bayesian weight tuning and a longitudinal-control case study, but detailed evaluation setup and results remain unresolved.

unresolved_questions: Inspect the full paper for service graph, control-error/computation metrics, deadline model, optimization overhead and execution platform.

editorial.why_now_note: Runtime service composition is relevant to SDV software architecture because it turns allocation/composition decisions into an online control-plane function.
editorial.rationale: Useful conceptual runtime-orchestration evidence, but the current verification depth is insufficient for architecture-wide performance conclusions.
